key_insight: PhysMiner automates turbulence-physics discovery by combining shear-insensitive triple decomposition with LLM-based reasoning to identify flow mechanisms more reliably than conventional gradient analysis.
engineering_relevance: The framework can improve turbulence modeling and subgrid-scale model development for complex engineering flows by extracting physically consistent structures and recommendations automatically.
method: Triple-decomposes velocity gradients into rigid rotation, pure shearing, and normal straining to remove shear contamination.
Runs automated statistics, contour visualization, vortex-line extraction, and threshold-insensitive vortex identification.
Uses a discover-physics agent plus a review agent, with a growing library for cross-case knowledge accumulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation across five benchmarks and an end-to-end demonstration on periodic hill flow, where the system produced improved Reynolds-stress predictions and turbulence-modeling recommendations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of agent reasoning and library growth, so physical conclusions may still require expert scrutiny for novel or highly noisy flows.
paper_title: PhysMiner: An Agentic AI Framework for Discovering Turbulence Physics
